subject: represent an absent factor with geom_bar

messages.author: 3c30c52b0f668f28
messages.subject: represent an absent factor with geom_bar
parts:
Hello ggplot useRs,

mtcars$cyl.f <- factor(mtcars$cyl, c(2, 4, 6, 8), c(2, 4, 6, 8))
summary(mtcars$cyl.f)
 2  4  6  8
 0 11  7 14

c <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(x=cyl.f))
c + geom_bar()

The graph produce with geom_bar have 3 bars, and it's normal... But I would like the factor "2" to be represented on the x-axis, like on this graph :

 barplot(table(mtcars$cyl.f))

Thank you for help.

David

On Fri, Feb 13, 2009 at 10:10 AM, David Hajage <dha...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hello ggplot useRs,
>
> mtcars$cyl.f <- factor(mtcars$cyl, c(2, 4, 6, 8), c(2, 4, 6, 8))
> summary(mtcars$cyl.f)
> 2 4 6 8
> 0 11 7 14
>
> c <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(x=cyl.f))
> c + geom_bar()
>
> The graph produce with geom_bar have 3 bars, and it's normal... But I would
> like the factor "2" to be represented on the x-axis, like on this graph :
>
> barplot(table(mtcars$cyl.f))

Just set the x axis limits:

c + geom_bar() + xlim("2","4","6","8")
